review_method: model-assisted cross-check of the cited public primary-source pages; not an independent human audit, frozen source snapshot, or proof of all the publishers' mathematical assumptions
scope: Published displayed equations and explicitly stated domains only. Generated lean candidate translation fidelity requires separate kernel comparison plus source review.

findings.explanation: The commutative law of addition is printed for real a,b.
The parenthesized associative law of addition is printed for real a,b,c.
The commutative law of multiplication uses a dot product on real scalars.
The distributive law matches the textbook's displayed equation.
The additive-identity equation is printed for every real a.
The multiplicative-identity equation is printed for every real a.
OpenStax prints a + (-a) = 0; the structural frontend emits a + (0 - a) = 0, requiring zero_sub rather than rfl.
DLMF 1.2.3 is the sum of binomial coefficients to 2^n with n a nonnegative integer; the oracle uses Nat.choose.
DLMF 1.2.7 uses generalized binomial coefficients with complex z and integral k; do not substitute Nat.choose.
DLMF 1.2.37 is transpose of product; the reference uses matrices over ℂ with conformable dimensions, not an arbitrary-scalar theorem.
Nicholson Theorem 2, property 2 states transpose involution; the typed reference restricts to real matrices.
Nicholson Theorem 2, property 4 states transpose additivity for matrices of the same size; typed reference restricts to real matrices.

limitations: Publisher pages are live web resources without a timestamp-pinned page snapshot.
OpenStax LaTeX was transcribed and wrapped in new theorem documents, not copied from a publisher source repository.
Typed DLMF and Nicholson matrix propositions are field specializations; they do not certify arbitrary-domain interpretations.
D02 has no typed source oracle and no source-faithfulness credit.
Equivalence of two true propositions is insufficient evidence of faithful translation; only restrictive kernel-rechecked normalization is used.
